full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman, J: Plaintiff- petitioner filed an application before the Sub ordinance Judge, Chandpur in Title Suit No. 85 of 1990 for staying all further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 6 of 1985, arising out of a suit for partition, being Partition Suit No. 53 of 1958. The trial Judge rejected this application by his order dated 17.2.91. This order was unsuccessfully challenged before the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 949 of 1991. Plaintiff- petitioner now seeking leave to appeal from the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. 

 2. One Yeasin Bhuiya son of late Mondir Mahmud filed Partition Suit No. 53 of 1958 and the same was decreed in preliminary form on 23.5.59 and the final decree was passed on 24.9.85. Thereafter Title Execution Case No. 6 of 1985 was started for exaction of the final decree. After passing of the final decree in that partition suit one Asia Khatoon filed Title Suit No. 153 of 1985 for a declaration that the decree passed in the partition suit's void, illegal and not binding on her and for setting aside the judgment and decree of that partition suit. In that suit Asia Khatoon prayed for staying the further proceeding of Title Execution Case No. 6 of 1985 and stay was granted. After the disposal of the aforesaid suit, the stay of Title Execution Case No. 6 of 1985 was vacated. Asia Khatoon being old her son in law Md. Adbul Momen, her constituted attorney filed Tide Suit No. 85 of 1990 for a declaration that the solenama that was Filed on 25.10.90 in Title Suit No. 153 of 1985 was illegal, void and collusive and for setting aside the dismissal order. Asia Khatuns Attorney also prayed for stay of the proceeding of Title Execution Case No. 6 of 1985 and the same was rejected. Subsequently, the High Court Division affirmed the order of rejection of the Subordinate Judge; Chandpur. 

 4. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division found that admittedly the suit property originally belonged to one Mandir Mahmud and that all his successors were made parties in the partition suit including the husband of Asia Khatoon, Md. Ibrahim son of Soleman one of the daughters of Mandir Mahmud. The learned Single Judge correctly held that Asia Khatun being the wife of Md. Ibrahim was not at all a co-sharer in the suit land and consequently she was not a necessary party in the partition suit. Further, it appears that Asia Khatun filed successive suits to frustrate the decree obtained in Partition Suit No.53 of 1958. The learned Single Judge correctly found that the approach of the present plaintiff in staying further proceeding of Title Execution Case No. 6 of 1985 was not bonafide. Whether the execution case should be stayed or not is purely a matter of judicial discretion for the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division. Proper discretion having been exercised on the materials on record, the same calls for no interference.
